title: The Midnight Menagerie
subtitle: Twelve stolen animals. Nine working machines. Choose your math level: grades 5-8.
briefing: Baron Bramble has stolen twelve animals from the woodland sanctuary. Slip inside his moonlit castle, explore the courtyards, and outsmart the mechanisms that keep them penned up. Every animal you free will follow you. Get the whole rescue team to the river boat.
setting: A make-believe castle. A very real need for your math skills.
finale: The last boat slips into the reeds just as the sun rises. All 12 animals are back at the woodland sanctuary. Baron Bramble finds empty pens, open locks, and one small note: Animals belong at home.

steps.title: The balance vault
steps.story: Bramble has sealed the outer gate with three connected balance mechanisms. Step into the gate workshop. Rebuild each fixed load with the loose weights to align all three release pins.
steps.success: Three seals released. The castle gate is open!
steps.explanation: Equivalent loads aligned all three balance pins. Fractions, decimals and mixed numbers describe the same physical mass.

steps.title: Patrol synchronizer
steps.story: Find the FIRST positive tick when every wheel hole returns to its release line. The wheels turn once every 4, 6 ticks. Zero does not count.
steps.success: All the holes align at the first possible moment. The lookout shutter closes!

introductionTitle: Twelve animals. One secret way out.

previewWeeks.title: Open the courtyard
previewWeeks.setting: At the outer gate, equalize the loads and find the patrol's first shared opening.

sessions.product: Three weight arrangements that balance the gate's fraction, decimal, and mixed-number mechanisms.
sessions.sample: A prepared weight tray and fixed pan loads are ready to rearrange.

sessions.product: A tested crank setting that aligns the lookout's patrol wheels at their first shared opening.
sessions.sample: The patrol wheels start at zero with all crank settings available.

questions: Which quantities are equivalent even though their labels look different? Use the pan readings to explain.
How would moving or removing one weight change the equality? What could restore the balance?
When will both patrol wheels align? Why is a later alignment not the first opening?
Which failed trial helped you revise your setup, and what would you test next?

Crank step count, wheel periods, alignment readings, and earlier attempts.

previewWeeks.title: Repair the clockwork

sessions.product: A complete fraction cog with one whole of coverage and no overlapping sectors.

sessions.product: A calibrated compound gear train with tested cog sizes and input turns.
sessions.sample: The gear inventory and drive train are prepared; fit cogs to axles A and B.

questions: How do the sectors add to one whole? Why can a sum of one still leave a jammed wheel?
What common unit helps compare these fraction pieces?
How do tooth counts change axle speed and direction? Predict the output before cranking.
Which cog or crank revision changed the result? How would a new output target change your setup?

controls: Sector inventory, ring divisions, tooth counts, and scaffolding.
Gear multipliers, drive/pinion teeth, crank range, output target, and grade pathway.

previewWeeks.title: Build the way out
previewWeeks.setting: Send a moonbeam through the tower, then position and tension the rescue bridge.

sessions.product: A mirror relay that sends the moonbeam to its receiver around the tower obstacles.

sessions.product: A bridge alignment and cable choice tested in both the positioning engine and tension carriage.

questions: How does turning a mirror change the outgoing ray? Which angle measurement helps predict its path?
What coordinates place the bridge head on its target? How does a translation change each coordinate?
